tasks.short: Write and check the design for a people report before anyone builds it.

today.trigger: An HR business partner, a site manager or the controller asks for a report, or an AFAS field, a CAO rule or a definition of verzuim or day-90 retention changes an existing one.
steps: Write down the decision the report must support, the population, and the split by site, CAO, own staff and flex.
Look up the fields in the nightly AFAS extract and, where the question needs them, in Recruitee, Studytube or the agency hour files.
Draft the spec on SharePoint: grain, filters, measures, the nightly refresh, and who may see which site and which contract type.
Check hour, headcount and verzuim definitions with the Payroll Specialist or the controller, and keep medical absence content out of the spec.
File the spec, then build the Power BI change or hand the spec on.
drudgery: Retyping column names, filters and row-level roles that already sit in the model.
Rewriting the same population and access paragraphs for every report.
Hunting an old Word spec that has drifted from the published report.
today.time_sinks: Most of the 51.5 hours sits in agreeing what a hire, a day-90 stayer and verzuim mean across HR, payroll and finance, then making the written spec match the model people actually open.

lenses.faster: The field list, the access section and the measure text are filled from the model and the definition catalogue, and the analyst edits that draft. The review with payroll or the controller stays.
lenses.autonomous: A new request, or a change in the AFAS extract or a published measure, opens a draft spec and a diff against the last approved version on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would keep a current spec for every North Star report and every site pack, including the reports that were built in a hurry and never written down.
lenses.joy: Copying column names into Word is the part nobody would miss. The work that remains is settling what counts as a productive warehouse hire at day 90.
lenses.options: Each request comes back as three specs: one page for the shift manager, one split by CAO and by own staff versus flex, and one set of counts and rates for the works council.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the definition catalogue, the spec template and the check that a published report still matches its spec.
reach: The controller's monthly note that reconciles HR headcount with finance headcount per site.
The payroll specialist's check that a reported hour type matches the goods-transport CAO or the warehouse CAO.
The FP&A analyst's workforce-cost bridge, once both sides use the same contract-type rules.
The learning specialist's coverage extract for forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates from Studytube.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst is the one who can pick a population and a definition that payroll, the HR business partners and the works council will stand behind, and who can stop a design that would show health data or score a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Model metadata and the definition catalogue can fill most of a spec, and a checker can test that every section and measure is present. The spec is the order to build, so a person approves it before anyone acts on it.

in_practice.trigger: A report request lands on a SharePoint list or a Teams channel, or a job detects a change in the AFAS extract schema or in a Power BI measure.
steps: Read the request against the catalogue entries for hire, day-90 retention, verzuim, contract type, site and CAO.
List the matching columns, measures and row-level roles. When a spec already exists, diff it against the current model and catalogue.
Draft or update the spec in the SharePoint template, including gaps, the nightly refresh, and a flag when any figure would score a person.
Mark clashes with the two CAOs, with AVG access for own staff and flex workers, and with works-council consent where the report would track individuals.
Route the draft to the analyst, and also to Payroll or the controller when hours, verzuim or headcount definitions change.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the spec before the report is built or changed. Payroll or the controller co-approves when the definition of hours, verzuim or headcount changes.
data_needed: AFAS extract data dictionary and the scope of the nightly refresh.
Current Power BI measures, relationships and row-level security roles.
Approved definitions for hire, day-90, verzuim, contract type, site and CAO.
The request text and the decision the report must support.
A list of medical, disciplinary and agency-confidential fields that stay out of manager views.
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint spec library keeps the version history, and a report register row stores the request, the model version, the approver and the date.

evidence.claim: A Power BI dataset already stores measure expressions, relationships and security roles that can be listed without retyping them into a spec.
AFAS Profit exposes HR, absence, contract and payroll data through GetConnectors and scheduled extracts, which is the feed this company's nightly Power BI refresh already depends on.
Dutch works councils have a consent right on arrangements for tracking personnel, so some people-report designs are a consultation item as well as a technical note.
Filling a design template from metadata is plausible, and the share of these 51.5 hours that is writing rather than definition meetings is not known for this company.

risks: A wrong verzuim or day-90 formula, once accepted in the template, gets copied into every later report.
A manager role sees individual absence notes, or flex-worker fields the agency arrangement does not allow the company to spread.
A report that tracks individuals goes live and the works council hears about it afterwards.
Managers keep a private Excel copy and the SharePoint spec, and month-end uses whichever is convenient.
A design that adds a leavers or absence score is documented as an ordinary report and skips an EU AI Act and works-council check.
research_questions: Of the 51.5 hours a year, how many are drafting and how many are meetings to agree definitions with payroll, finance and HR business partners?
Can a script running inside the company read the Power BI model and the AFAS extract dictionary under the current AVG arrangements?
Which report changes already need payroll, controller or works-council sign-off before they are published?
What share of published people reports have a spec that still matches the measures in the model?

tasks.short: Scan HR tool changes and pick which people reports to build or drop.

today.trigger: AFAS, Power BI, Recruitee or Studytube ships a change, report use on a site drops, or the HR Director asks what HR should build next. For this seat the products are the people reports and HR services the three sites use.
steps: Read release notes from AFAS, Power BI, Recruitee and Studytube, plus public notes on EU rules for employment software.
Check which Power BI reports managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo actually open, and which North Star figures are still disputed.
Write a short mail or Word note on what Noordhaven can use with the current AFAS extract and what would be a new build.
Talk the shortlist through with the HR Director and, when it touches cost or headcount, with the controller or an FP&A analyst.
Park the rejected ideas on a SharePoint list.
drudgery: Reading vendor announcements to find the one paragraph that applies to Profit and to a nightly extract.
Explaining the same three tools again each quarter.
Keeping a trend note that the HR Director cannot find later.
today.time_sinks: The slow part is separating a change Noordhaven can use from a feature that needs data the nightly extract does not have, a second CAO rule, or works-council consent.

lenses.faster: A fixed source list is read and scored against the North Star and the systems Noordhaven already runs, and the analyst starts from a one-page shortlist. The decision meeting stays.
lenses.autonomous: A release from AFAS, Power BI, Recruitee or Studytube, or a month in which a standard report is barely opened, files that shortlist on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a backlog of unanswered workforce questions per site and per CAO, and would retire reports that managers leave unopened.
lenses.joy: Vendor webinars are the part nobody would miss. The part worth keeping is choosing the one change a site manager or an HR business partner would feel in the next quarter.
lenses.options: The brief holds five options. Each one shows the build hours, whether the data is already in the nightly extract, the works-council or AVG gate, and the metric it would move.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the source list, the scoring rules and the reasons to reject an item, and reviews the shortlist.
reach: The FP&A analyst's scan of workforce-cost drivers for the next forecast, using the same contract types.
The learning specialist's watch on certificate rules for forklift, VCA and food safety that Studytube already records.
The recruiter's question on which Recruitee stages still have no governed timing.
The controller's question on whether a new AFAS function would remove an Excel bridge in the pay cycle.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows what a three-site operator with two CAOs, three staffing agencies and a works council can absorb this quarter, and can stop a proposal that would rank employees.
tasks.pattern_why: Collecting public release notes and scoring them against a fixed system list and the North Star is a multi-step job a person should not retype. A recommendation can affect employees, so the analyst approves the brief before the HR Director treats it as the plan.

in_practice.trigger: A watched public source publishes a change, Power BI usage for a standard report falls below an agreed line, or the month ends with no material release.
steps: Pull new items from an allowed list: AFAS Profit releases, Power BI releases, Recruitee, Studytube, agency-portal changes, and public EU or Dutch notes on employment software.
Drop items that need data Noordhaven does not hold, or that would score or rank an employee.
Score what remains against time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, day-90 retention, verzuim, and hours currently spent on Excel bridges.
Draft a one-page brief with at most five options, each with effort, site or CAO scope, and the consent or privacy gate.
Attach aggregate usage of the current reports so a weak report can be retired as well as extended.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the brief before it goes to the HR Director. Any item that would monitor or score employees carries a written note that works-council consent and an AVG purpose check come first.
data_needed: The allowed source list and confirmation that those texts may be processed under the company AVG arrangements.
The inventory of systems this seat actually has: AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube, Power BI, agency portals.
North Star definitions and the current gaps in each one.
Aggregate Power BI usage by report and by site, with no employee-level rows.
Known works-council and AVG boundaries, including flex-worker data from the three agencies.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint backlog list stores the source, the score, the decision, the date and the name of the person who approved the brief.

evidence.claim: Power BI can show how often a published report is opened, which is a direct signal of whether an existing people report earns its keep.
AFAS publishes Profit release notes that describe functional changes an HRIS analyst can read against the modules the company uses.

Employment software that profiles or scores people sits in a stricter EU AI Act category than a descriptive headcount or verzuim rate. The exact obligation date for a given dashboard should be checked against the official text before anyone relies on it.
A scheduled digest that scores public release notes against an internal metric list is a plausible build. No documented case at a Dutch logistics employer was identified.

risks: Vendor release text is treated as proof that a feature works on Noordhaven's AFAS setup and nightly extract.
A proposal to predict who will leave or who will be absent is passed on as an ordinary report improvement.
The brief is produced every month and the HR Director still chooses the backlog in the management meeting, so the hours saved come back as unread pages.
An agent that also opens SharePoint policies, OR papers or employee files would send personal data to a model the company has not assessed.
Time goes into logistics-market questions that sit with commercial colleagues, while hire-to-day-90 and verzuim stay unresolved.
research_questions: Does this analyst actually spend about 45 hours a year on tool and trend scanning, or does that O*NET time in practice go to report builds and ad hoc questions?
Which sources may be processed by a model under the current AVG arrangements, and which folders are out of bounds?
If a five-item brief had existed over the last year, which items would the HR Director have funded, and which metrics would have moved?
Have managers already asked for individual absence-risk or flight-risk scores, and has the works council set a boundary on that?

role.altitude: The owner of the people-data definitions and of the short list of reports that serve hire-to-productive, absence-to-return and the pay cycle. Specs and tool scans become outputs of that system.
reach: FP&A workforce-cost bridges that use the same headcount, site and contract-type rules.
The controller's check that HR headcount and finance headcount match per site after the nightly refresh.
Learning and development views of forklift, VCA and food-safety certificate coverage from Studytube.
Governed Recruitee stage timings for the two recruiters, in place of a separate funnel spreadsheet.
A payroll check when a report hour and the payslip disagree under either CAO.
A narrow read of agency hours against agency invoices for the bookkeepers, once flex hours sit in the same model.
role.ceiling_note: These two tasks are about 96 hours a year inside a one-person seat loaded at EUR 78 an hour. The ceiling is the rest of that year, the quality of the nightly AFAS extract, the two CAOs, works-council consent, and AVG limits on flex-worker and health data. One analyst cannot be the data steward on three sites and also close payroll.
skills_to_grow: Power BI semantic-model review: grain, measures and row-level security on the AFAS extract.
A definition of time to hire, day-90 retention and verzuim that payroll and finance will both use.
AVG and works-council boundaries for people reports, including data from the three staffing agencies.
Enough SQL or Python to test a population rule against the extract.
A working test for whether a request is a descriptive report or a score that needs an EU AI Act and works-council check.
role.ambitious_version: Every input to the North Star has one definition, one population rule and one nightly figure that the three sites, HR and finance all use. Specs are generated from that catalogue and checked against the model. The analyst's year goes into the definitions that are still disputed, the reports managers leave unopened, and the requests that should be refused because they would rank workers or put medical content on a verzuim dashboard.
